details:
Q1: What should the main fix be?
Choices:
A) Hardening without a new container, in three layers:
   - Remove or deny the risky `git` forms in `READ_PROFILE_ALLOW`: `--output`, `-O`/`--open-files-in-pager`, `--ext-diff`, `--textconv`, and their abbreviations.
   - Make the support checkout non-writable before the model runs.
   - Fail closed right before any support script runs if the support checkout is not clean at the approved commit (`git status --porcelain` empty and HEAD equals the approved SHA). (RECOMMENDED)
B) Full OS sandbox: run read-profile Claude calls in a read-only, network-isolated container with the host-side model broker, the same way `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` does. No change to the allow list or the integrity checks.
C) Both A and B in this issue. This is a much larger change across several workflows.
Q2: Which callers should get the fix?
Choices:
A) All host-side read-profile roles. The allow-list hardening applies everywhere anyway, because `READ_PROFILE_ALLOW` is shared. The integrity check goes before support-script execution in every workflow that runs a read-profile Claude call on the host and then runs support scripts: `security-audit.yml` (SECURITY_AUDIT), the orchestrator poller (SECURITY_JUDGE), and workflow-failure-heal intake (WORKFLOW_HEAL). (RECOMMENDED)
B) Only the security-audit path named in the finding: the shared allow-list change plus the integrity check in `security-audit.yml`. Other callers get separate follow-up issues.
